title: What We Owe the Soil
lead: Steward Tull stands up in council with a jar of grey dust from the Sundial's east field, and says the soil is dying. Then she says the fleet has put two thousand good fields out of the airlock since the Fall, and that she'd like to discuss it.
anyone: Steward Tull stood up in council with a jar of grey dust from the Sundial's east field, and said the soil is dying. Then she said the fleet has put two thousand good fields out of the airlock since the Fall, and that she'd like to discuss it.

gm.truth: She's right, and she has hidden it for months by blending the grain, because the harvest is the only power she has. Old ore dust in the Sundial's hold is leaching up through the beds, and within four or five harvests yields collapse. She's saying it now because Imre Katz's figures are about to get out, and if she says it first, it's an argument and not a scandal. On the Sundial the dead have always gone to the common compost: clean organic matter binds the metals and rebuilds a bed. The rest of the fleet gives its dead to the void, and she wants them. There's no conspiracy here: it's the ugliest public argument in the fleet's short history, and every people has a stake. Veshti are horrified: a Veshti goes to the void, and being put in dirt is the worst thing they've ever heard of. Korrun want to be weighed first. Thessan want a record of every atom. Synthetics ask, dryly, whether their metals are wanted too. Father Roe has to speak for a Service he doesn't believe in. Oskar Lind says everyone is kept anyway, his followers line up to volunteer, and this makes everyone else recoil. Anton Reyk, a retired surveyor, comes to the captain because his wife died this morning, she loved the beans, and he wants her to go in the ground. Their daughter Lisbet says she'll stop him.
beats: The jar of dust in council. She sets it on Speaker Halm's desk, adds a carrot and sits down. Halm is delighted for about a minute, and then he understands what the question is. It goes on the agenda for next week.
The fleet argues. A Veshti delegation comes to the captain in formal dress. Korrun on Deck Four start asking what a person weighs. Someone paints WE ARE NOT FERTILIZER on a grain barge.
Anton and Lisbet Reyk, with a body in the cold room and until tomorrow to decide. He asks the captain to come and say something. She asks the captain to stop it.
The science. Imre Katz on the Sundial shows how bad it is and how long there is. It's worse than Grann said. Grann was being generous.
The first burial or the vote or both, with every ship listening.
routes: The open argument: persuasion and leadership in council and on Garrick Fenn's channel. A voluntary system, a mandatory one or none at all, each with a real constituency.

Find another way: science and survival for clean soil from somewhere else, with commerce to pay for it: a Cinder Reach mineral cargo, or Tessen's living soil, which means Grann Tull asking Elder Dray for something after thirty-four years. It could buy a harvest or two.

The customs: lore to find what the old rites really require, and what each people could live with. The Veshti have an old word for being returned to the ship's own water, unused for centuries, and it might be a way through.
The family: persuasion and composure with the Reyks at the cold room, one father and one daughter, no politics in it. Whichever way it goes, the fleet will take its cue from this.
checks: survival:moderate to read the soil and see how long it really has
science:hard to find enough clean soil anywhere else
lore:moderate to find the old Veshti term for returning to the ship's water
persuasion:hard to bring a Veshti delegation back to the table
leadership:very_hard to speak at the first burial and be heard by every ship
composure:moderate to stand between Anton and Lisbet Reyk
fights: desperate_refugee crowd tearing up the east field, if it goes badly
outcomes: Voluntary: some sign up and many don't, and it covers about two-thirds of what's needed. People write down a row number. Children know where their grandparents are. Over time it becomes the first custom in the fleet that belongs to nobody else.

Mandatory: the soil is saved, and the council has just told every Veshti in the fleet what will be done with their mother. The Veshti ships may not stay. Some families hide their dead or give them to the void at night, and that's a crime now.
Refused: the rites go on as they were. Grann nods, says nothing and goes back to blending the grain. In a few harvests the captain will have to explain to thirty thousand people what the jar meant.
Another way found: it's only a harvest or two, and it costs a lot. The question is put off. It will be back, and the same jar will be sitting on the same table.
gm.rewards: Grann's respect, which is rare, nutrient_gel crates from a grateful Sundial, and standing with whichever peoples the captain stood with.
